summary.text: Bruce Blakeman is the Nassau County Executive, elected in 2021, and the Republican and Conservative Party nominee for governor with running mate Todd Hood. An attorney, he previously served on the Nassau County Legislature and the Hempstead Town Council, was a Port Authority commissioner, and lost races for state comptroller (1998), U.S. Senate (2010 primary) and Congress (2014). His campaign centers on rolling back congestion pricing, cutting taxes, and public safety, building on a record as county executive that includes freezing county property taxes, hiring hundreds of additional police officers, and an executive order — later struck down and reenacted as a county law that is being challenged in court — banning transgender athletes from girls' and women's sports at county facilities. He describes himself as a pro-choice Republican.

paragraphs.text: Born in Oceanside and raised in Valley Stream, Nassau County, according to the county executive's official biography; born in 1955, per Wikipedia.

Earned a B.A. from Arizona State University and a J.D. from California Western School of Law; he is an attorney admitted to practice in New York and New Jersey and before the U.S. Supreme Court and other federal courts, and worked as a partner at his father's law firm.
According to the county biography, he has served as Executive Director of the New York Police Chiefs Benevolent Association and as Deputy Counsel to the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Foundation.
Served on the Hempstead Town Council from 1993 to 1995 and again from 2015 to 2021.
Served on the Nassau County Legislature representing the 7th district, elected as the body's first presiding officer, and lost his seat in the November 1999 election.
Was the Republican nominee for New York State Comptroller in 1998, losing to incumbent Democrat Carl McCall.
Served as a Commissioner of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, appointed by the Governor of New York in 2001 in the aftermath of the September 11 attacks, until 2009.

Lost the 2010 Republican primary for U.S. Senate to Joe DioGuardi and then ran on the Tax Revolt line in the general election; won the Republican nomination for New York's 4th Congressional District in 2014 but lost the general election to Kathleen Rice, 52.8% to 47.1%.
Elected Nassau County Executive on November 2, 2021, defeating incumbent Democrat Laura Curran; took office January 1, 2022, becoming the county's first Jewish county executive.
According to the county biography, he lives in Atlantic Beach with his wife, Segal.
